Bank ledger integrity violations by category
HTTP error codes by application/code
panels.description: All bounded RFC-7807 error codes (basetool_http_error_total) by application and code. The 0.1 threshold marks the OptimisticLockConflictSpike alert level for the dedicated OPTIMISTIC_LOCK series.

panels.title: Item-order line blueprint drift
panels.description: REQ-ORDERS-033: ordered-item lines whose blueprint no longer produces the ordered item after an SC-Wiki re-point. > 0 means those orders display a foreign recipe as their material demand; the backend log names each affected order, and re-saving an order re-derives its lines.

panels.title: Ingest handoff rate by kind
panels.description: Staged handoffs/s per HandoffKind (basetool_ingest_handoff_total): an exchange client's draft (REFINERY, BLUEPRINT) or a change set the mass-change guard held back (MASS_CHANGE).

panels.title: Ingest gateway errors by reason
panels.description: Ingest gateway failures/s by reason (basetool_ingest_handoff_errors_total): staging_unavailable = Redis refused a staged draft or change set, internal = an unexpected 500. Relay failures to the backend are counted as basetool_ingest_exchange_relay_total{outcome="failed"}. Backs IngestHandoffErrors / IngestStagingUnavailable.

panels.title: Ingest gateway error ratio (10m)
panels.description: Share of staging attempts and unexpected failures against staged handoffs over 10m.

panels.title: Audit events (last 60d) by domain (review of the non-alerted domains)
Discord precheck/hour by outcome
panels.description: Keycloak SPI account-existence prechecks per hour by outcome (basetool_discord_precheck_total: ok / unauthorized / disabled). The endpoint sits outside /api/**, outside the rate limiter and outside the basetool_http_error funnel, so without this counter a secret-guessing attempt or a shared secret broken by rotation is log-only (#1041 item 19). The counter is created on first use, so an EMPTY panel is the ordinary state: no Discord-linked registration has been attempted since the last backend restart. What matters is the shape once it does populate -- a rising `unauthorized` line is the signal, and DiscordPrecheckUnauthorizedSpike alerts on it.

targets.expr: sum by (application, bucket) (rate(basetool_ratelimit_rejections_total[10m])) / sum by (application, bucket) (rate(basetool_ratelimit_requests_total[10m]))

panels.title: Live-sync subscribe outcomes/hour by topic class
panels.description: Multiplexed /ws/sync subscribe-authorization verdicts per topic class (REQ-FE-015, ADR-0094). A rising `denied` rate on a room every viewer should reach hints at an auth/gate regression; `allowed` includes transient fail-open.

panels.title: Live-sync subscriptions (live) by topic class
panels.description: Open /ws/sync topic subscriptions per topic class on this instance (basetool_livesync_subscriptions). The concurrent live-sync load denominator per surface; a flatline while sessions are active hints the socket or a room's subscribe is broken.

panels.title: Live-sync changed relay/hour by topic class
panels.description: Peer-forwarded `changed` frames per topic class (the per-surface breakdown of panel 28). A `changed` flatline is only meaningful when read against panel 47 (peer rooms): a room with one viewer relays zero frames by design, because relayLocal skips the origin. A flatline WHILE that class holds peer rooms is the early indicator of the REQ-FE-010 stale-peer defect class; a flatline with no peer rooms just means nobody was co-editing. The positive detector for the same defect is the LiveSyncSectionKeySkew alert (#1238), which needs no occupancy assumption.

panels.title: Redis fan-out pub/sub & errors/hour
panels.description: Cross-replica Redis fan-out for live delivery (ADR-0094/ADR-0126): the live-sync changed-relay (basetool_livesync_redis_*), the editor-presence gossip (basetool_livesync_presence_*) and the notification SSE fan-out (basetool_sse_redis_*). Publishing is fire-and-forget after the local relay/broadcast, so a rising `errors` stream means cross-replica delivery is silently degraded to single-instance — watched by the LiveSyncRedisFanoutBroken alert, which covers the changed relay and the SSE fan-out only (a lost changed frame costs correctness; a lost presence gossip costs a cosmetic dot, so it is a panel row, not a page). Note the presence rows are a PERIODIC gossip — one message per actively-edited topic per 10 s per replica — so a steady non-zero floor is normal there and a flat zero simply means nobody has a mission panel focused. Which rows CAN populate depends on how many processes sit on the channel, and the difference is invisible in the panel: basetool_sse_redis_consumed_total counts peer-origin messages only (own-origin excluded), and production runs a single backend replica -- so that row, and its errors row, are permanently absent here and their absence is correct. The live-sync rows do populate on the same single-replica host, because backend and frontend are two DIFFERENT processes on one channel. Read side by side, one bridge looks alive and the other looks dead while both are healthy; a genuinely broken SSE fan-out shows up as `published` continuing while notifications stop arriving, not as this row going flat (the #1488 lesson, on a second metric).

panels.title: Session evictions/hour
panels.description: Concurrent-session evictions (basetool_session_evicted_total): Spring Security expired a principal's oldest session because the per-user cap of 10 was full. The panel sits beside 'Active sessions' on purpose - the gauge cannot show this, because expireNow() only marks the session and leaves the registry entry and the Redis key in place. Rare by construction; a floor that never returns to zero means the registry is holding dead sessions against the cap and evicting live ones (watched by SessionEvictionSpike).

panels.title: Browser client errors/hour by kind
panels.description: Browser-side failures posted by the client error beacon (basetool_client_error_total, kind = script_error / unhandled_rejection / resource_error / csp_violation / i18n_missing). An i18n_missing is a localized string a script needed and the page did not provide; the UI shows the key name instead (window.krtI18nText, since 2026-09-23). A csp_violation is something the Content-Security-Policy blocked in the browser (an inline script or style without the nonce, a host the policy does not allow); the CSP has no report-uri, so this beacon is its only signal. A JS exception that kills a krtFetch handler issues no request at all, so it appears in no other panel on this dashboard. Read the shape, not the level: a low permanent background is normal (old browsers, extensions, tabs open across a deploy), a step in one kind that starts at a deploy and stays up is the broken live-update surface (watched by ClientErrorSpike).

panels.title: External catalogue fetch errors/hour by source
panels.description: Swallowed UEX / SC-Wiki fetch, parse and pagination-contract failures (basetool_external_fetch_errors_total). Each is mapped to an empty or incomplete result, so the sync job still records success and the staleness alerts stay quiet. For scwiki this doubles as the only proxy for 'the scwiki_deleted orphan sweep stood down this run': an incomplete page walk always contributes one increment here. A burst trips ExternalFetchErrors; a line that is non-zero on every daily run trips ScWikiCensusIncompleteStreak, which means orphan detection has been off for days (in 2026-08 that was a defect in the census check itself, not the feed — ADR-0147).

panels.title: Live-sync peer rooms by topic class
panels.description: Rooms currently holding TWO OR MORE subscribers, per topic class (#1238) — the rooms in which peer-sync can actually do anything. Read panel 39 against this one: relayLocal skips the originating session, so a room with a single viewer relays zero `changed` frames however hard that viewer edits, which makes a `changed` flatline the normal state of an unoccupied surface rather than a defect. basetool_livesync_subscriptions cannot substitute — it sums sockets across a class, so two lone viewers in different rooms look identical to two peers in one. Measured over the 21d to 2026-08-03 co-presence is rare (peak concurrent subscriptions: mission 15, bank_staff 6, order_detail 4, others 3 or fewer, operation 1), which is why the per-topic_class changed-flatline alert stays deferred.

panels.title: Live-sync socket lifetime
panels.description: How long each /ws/sync socket stayed open, sampled when it closes (basetool_livesync_socket_lifetime_seconds). Every other live-sync meter counts events ON a socket; this one measures the socket. The signature to read is the mean or max collapsing toward a fixed value near a proxy timeout — that is an intermediary closing idle connections, and each close costs a reconnect, one subscribe-authorization probe per subscribed room and a page-wide resync, for every open tab. It happened: the edge's proxy_read_timeout is 90 s and the socket sent nothing at all, so every tab reconnected on a 90-second cadence and no meter here could see it. The handler now pings every socket every 30 s, and a parity test pins that interval to the edge timeout. NOT alertable — an ordinary navigation also ends a socket after seconds, so no threshold separates it from a teardown; read the panel, do not wait for a page.

panels.title: Ingest auth failures/hour by bearer error and path scope
panels.description: Every ingest 401 under its RFC 6750 bearer error code. The 401 itself logs at DEBUG only (scanner-flood protection on the public surface), so this is the sole signal an operator has when a client fails to authenticate. invalid_token covers bad signature, wrong issuer, expired AND failed audience - check the gateway config before assuming the client is at fault. no_credentials is a request that brought no Authorization header at all and is normally the only non-zero series here: the gateway's own root is probed with the http_2xx_or_401 blackbox module, so its 401 volume is a monitoring baseline rather than a threat (ADR-0173). Deliberately not alerted: unauthenticated probes are constant noise.

panels.title: Acting-member refusals/hour by reason
panels.description: Every refusal of an X-Ingest-On-Behalf-Of header, split by why (ADR-0129). The response body is byte-identical for all five reasons on purpose, so that a caller cannot use this endpoint to find out which subjects exist - which makes this panel the only place they are distinguishable. Read the reasons differently: member_not_live is usually an offboarded member whose connected application is still installed, but VARYING subjects mean somebody is enumerating user ids; not_a_gateway means either the allowlist does not match the gateway's client id (exchange relays are failing too) or somebody is probing for an impersonation primitive; no_authenticated_caller should be structurally impossible and indicates the security filter chain was reordered.

panels.title: DPoP replay-cache refusals/hour by path scope and reason
panels.description: DPoP proofs the gateway's jti replay cache refused, per path scope (exchange / other) and reason: replayed (the jti was used before), member_cap (the member already holds its app.exchange.limits.dpop-proofs-per-member live proofs) or full (the scope's cache holds dpop-proofs-total and refuses every new proof; IngestDpopReplayCacheFull fires). On the exchange scope a member_cap refusal is answered 429 DPOP_PROOF_LIMIT and counts as dpop_proof_limit on the auth-failure counter, and a full refusal is answered 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE and counts as dpop_store_full; every other refusal counts as invalid_dpop_proof (REQ-XCH-006). The metric carries no client, so the client_id variable does not filter it.

panels.title: API requests/hour by client
panels.description: Which client software drives /api/** (A8, REQ-OBS-018). The label is bounded: a client the deployment does not know reads as 'other' (ApiUnknownClient alerts on it) and a token without an azp claim as 'none' — a Keycloak mapper regression that blinds the attribution, not a foreign caller. Anonymous requests are absent by design; they carry no client identity.

panels.title: Auth failures/hour by reason
panels.description: The cause behind the backend's 401s (A8, REQ-OBS-018, ADR-0173). no_credentials is a request that presented no Authorization header at all - the ordinary background, and normally the ONLY non-zero series: it is dominated by this deployment's own blackbox probes, which assert liveness by expecting a 401 on an allow-listed path (~0.1/s floor). invalid_token is a token that was presented and rejected (expired, wrong issuer/audience, bad signature) and is what BackendAuthFailureSpike watches, precisely because a probe or a scanner can never produce it. invalid_request is a malformed Authorization header, insufficient_scope a valid token missing a scope, other an unenumerated failure worth reading the DEBUG line for. Reading this beats raising a log level on a surface anonymous scanners can reach - but read the SPLIT, never the total: the total measures the monitoring plane.

panels.title: App live-sync streams (open)
panels.description: Open app live-sync SSE streams (ADR-0143). The app holds one per screen, so this tracks how many members are on a live surface. Evictions should sit at zero: a non-zero rate means a client is leaking streams on navigation rather than a member using four devices. Frames are written off the publishing thread through a bounded per-stream queue (BE-PERF-13): `queued` hovers near zero, and `dropped` counts frames refused by a full queue (AppLiveSyncFramesDropped).

targets.legendFormat: frames dropped at a full queue/h

panels.title: App live-sync publish outcomes/hour
panels.description: What the app announces after its own writes, and what was refused (ADR-0143). `no_known_sections` is a client bug; the two bucket reasons are the re-fetch-herd bounds doing their job. `consumed but not served` is the frontend's staff rooms crossing the shared channel — expected at a low steady rate, which is why it is not counted as an error.

panels.title: Erasures that left a Keycloak account (24h)
Accounts activated as admin without approval (7d)
Ingest audience gate enforcing
panels.description: Whether the ingest gateway's JWT audience check refuses tokens without aud=basetool-ingest (REQ-INGEST-011): 1 = enforcing, 0 = no audience configured, so any valid realm token passes the decoder. basetool_ingest_gate_enforcing{gate="audience"}; backs the IngestAudienceGateOff alert. The gate is switched on by the environment alone, so this panel is the only place the production posture is visible without reading the host.

panels.title: Exchange registry mirror writes/hour by phase and outcome
Exchange disconnects, departures and account checks/day
Exchange catalogue resolutions/hour by kind and status
Exchange gateway refusals/hour by reason
panels.description: Every exchange request the ingest gateway refused before it reached the backend, by problem code in snake case (REQ-XCH-028): DPoP, audience, registry, revocation, scope, version, limit, quota, idempotency and budget refusals. The per-client split is the panel beside the relay outcomes. Backs ExchangeDpopProofsFailing and ExchangeRegistryUnreadableAtGateway. The normal DPoP nonce round trip is no refusal and is not counted here; it shows as use_dpop_nonce on the ingest auth failures.

panels.title: Exchange writes/day by resource and outcome
panels.description: Ops external clients sent to the member's synced data (REQ-XCH-015…-017), by resource and outcome: applied, unchanged, unmatched, ambiguous or rejected; 'held' counts change sets the mass-change guard held back for the member's confirmation (REQ-XCH-021). The 'undo' series count the entries a member's undo restored or skipped (REQ-XCH-022). The 'confirmed' series count the held-back change sets members confirmed (REQ-XCH-021).

panels.title: Exchange requests/hour per client: refused and relayed by outcome
panels.description: The error picture of each registered client (REQ-XCH-028): gateway refusals and relayed requests by outcome, labelled client_id. Only registry clients carry their own id; any other token is 'unregistered', 'unknown' while the registry cannot be read, and refusals before a token was read are 'none' (not shown). The admin page Verbundene Anwendungen links here.

panels.title: Exchange Redis byte budget in use
panels.description: The share of the exchange's total Redis byte budget (64 MiB) the gateway's cached answers, quota counters and locks hold (REQ-XCH-023). Above 0.8 ExchangeBudgetHigh fires; at 1.0 writes are refused EXCHANGE_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED before they reach the backend.

panels.title: Exchange mass changes held for confirmation/day per client
panels.description: Change sets the backend's mass-change guard held back and the gateway staged for the member's confirmation in the browser (REQ-XCH-021), by registry client. A client that keeps tripping the guard is removing more than members expect.

panels.title: Security-expression failures/hour by kind
panels.description: Method-security expressions Spring Security could not evaluate (REQ-OBS-020). Every failure refused a call with 400 ILLEGAL_ARGUMENT. Normally flat zero: evaluation is a bean or method the expression names but the running context lacks (a renamed security bean, a changed arity), other an expression that yields no decision. Any point above zero fires SecurityExpressionEvaluationFailed; the WARN line of the 400 names the expression.
